title: Find the guessing floor as scored
statement: Work out each item's guessing floor from the scoring rule actually used where it is served, not from its format label.
example: A select-several item scored on its first choice had a floor of k/n, not the 1/C(n,k) its format implied.
detail: The reading course's practice spec states chance floors per item from its response declaration under the scoring rule actually serving it, after a live probe found scoring binary with no partial credit anywhere and multi-select scored as exact set equality (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). A select-k interaction authored as single cardinality was scored on its first token in the correct set, so its floor was k/n, not 1/C(n,k): the format label alone never determines the floor, and a bar within noise of its floor measures nothing (the same file).
